actions.init: Create the actual shipped ResourceProvider; minimal Django settings load class declarations without database IO
actions.create: ResourceProvider.create(); record returned name and object reference, do not supply or patch allocator
actions.delete: ResourceProvider.delete(name) for an emitted live identity
actions.reject-delete: ResourceProvider.delete(resource-0099), observe KeyError and retained live objects
actions.inspect: ResourceProvider.list() and actual returned object/name identity observations

limits: At most four creations and nine API transitions; two deletion orders, empty-provider recreation and rejected delete.
ResourceProvider is a shipped reference fake, not an external provider or database lifecycle.
Minimal Django settings permit importing the real module but make no database calls and do not patch creation/deletion in positive replay.
length-allocation compiles the actual create source with its counter increment changed to len(resources)+1.
copy-listed-objects is an explicit API-output mutation returning equal copies; detects loss of observable retained identity.
No liveness or full framework-version proof; historical audit.qnt remains unchanged.
